Each change has a _src note here and its pixels and arithmetic in TARGET-NOTES.md beside this file. Every other value is the lab's of 7 October (C:/Users/Jafar/ledger-lab/production/lab/2-sash-window/target.json), sourced in that folder's SOURCES.md. Second amendment, 8 October 2026, by another fresh helper (not the builder), for the first narrow point of the photograph review (production/audits/windows-2026-10-08/REVIEW-PHOTOGRAPHS.md, 'the glazing bar is too thin'): glazing_bar_width_mm 15.9 to 22.2 and bar_rebate_width_mm 4.8 to 6.4, measured on P6; each has a _src note here and its pixels and arithmetic in TARGET-NOTES.md, 'Second amendment: the glazing bar'. status: SOURCED 7 Oct 2026: Ellis, Modern Practical Joinery (1902) pp.121-127 (SOURCES.md [1]) unless noted; every value below has its line in SOURCES.md section 1. Inches as printed, millimetres for the code.

opening._src: Width 850: the game's street (brief of 8 Oct); was Ellis's 812.8 (2 ft 8 in, p.121); inside the book range 813 to 914 (SOURCES.md 1a). Height 1676.4 = 5 ft 6 in, Ellis p.121 Fig. 397 and Hasluck p.405 Fig. 1310, the ruling's 'period height of 1.68 m'; unchanged. Height over width 1.97: 1.4% under Rivington Part I p.193 ('from 2 to 2 1/2 times the breadth'), between Hasluck's worked example (1.83) and Ellis's (2.06).

frame._reveal: 4 1/2 in of brick before the outside lining, Ellis p.123 Fig. 400
frame._src_outer_lining_margin_mm: Was 19.1 (Ellis Fig. 400 scaled; Riley p.389). Now 1 11/16 in, so each jamb shows exactly 3 in of painted timber from the brick edge to the glass: 42.9 lining + (50.8 stile - 19.1 lining stop + 1.6 side play) 33.3 of stile = 76.2, the top of the ruling's 2.5 to 3 in. P6 (Tottenham, the only original in a brick reveal with a known size) shows about 51 mm of lining and 28 mm of stile, 79 mm (TARGET-NOTES.md). The width is carried by the outside lining showing further past the brick, as in P6: the pulley stile face now stands 23.8 inside the brick reveal line, not in line with it (Hasluck p.404); the lining still laps 65.1 behind the brick and still stands 19.1 proud of the pulley stile as the upper sash's stop, so Ellis's box, tracks and sashes are unchanged.
frame._olp: about 3/4 in past the pulley stile face, Riley p.389
frame._pb: 3/8 in nett, p.125; stands out about 7/8 in, scaled Fig. 400
frame._sb: 1 1/8 in deep, Fig. 400; stands out about 7/8 in, scaled
frame._src_head_visible_mm: Was 19.1 (Fig. 399). Now 1 3/4 in, so the head shows exactly 3 in: 44.5 head lining + (50.8 top rail - 19.1 behind the head lining) 31.7 = 76.2. P6's heads show at least 80 mm (lining 44 to 49 mm where lit, up to 77 with its shaded strip; top rail 36 to 38 mm; TARGET-NOTES.md). 1.6 more than the jambs' 42.9 because the head has no side play.

sash._t: '1 1/2 in' sashes finish 1 3/8 in, p.125; Fig. 400 label
sash._br: 'twice the width of top', p.127 (Fig. 399 reads 2 1/2 + 2 1/2; text used, SOURCES.md conflict 2)
sash._mr: 1 1/2 in, Fig. 399 (text 1 1/4 to 1 1/2). Kept 8 Oct: the photographs disagree (P6's face about 27 mm, Ellis Fig. 415's 1 1/8 in; P7 and P8 about 0.8 to 0.9 of the stile) and none shows a moulding on the outside face; P6's stepped look is this rail's underside and the lower rail seen from below (TARGET-NOTES.md)
sash._mrt: 'necessarily 3/8 in thicker than the stiles', p.127, to close the parting bead's gap
sash._horn: 3 in below the meeting rail, ogee, the stile's width, p.127 Figs. 415-416
sash._src_glazing_bar_width_mm: Was 15.9 (Ellis's 5/8 in bars, p.127). Now 7/8 in: the bar as seen from outside, painted fillet plus a putty bevel each side, glass edge to glass edge, which is what this value draws (target_drawing's elevation; window_design's bar with its putty inside the same width). P6, both upper-sash bars (the clearest), half-way points between glass and paint, 7-px row bands: left window rows 880, 940, 1000, 1040 = 34.0, 34.3, 34.0, 33.3 px; right window rows 880, 940, 1000 = 34.7, 35.0, 36.0 px; mean 34.5 px / 1.53 px/mm (TARGET-NOTES.md's brick scale, same rows) = 22.5 mm, +/-0.7 for the scale's 3%. P6's other bars: lower sashes 19 to 25 mm, the horizontal bar 18 to 24 mm; one run (right window, lower panes, 30 mm with a 20 mm fillet) looks repaired and is set aside. 22.2 is 0.3 under the clearest reading. Ellis names 'stouter bars' beside his 5/8 in (p.127); the lab's sources give 5/8 to 1 1/4 in (SOURCES.md 1, Riley).
sash._reb: rebate 1/4 in deep 'in all', p.127; width 1/4 to 1/2 in (Riley p.382), 3/8 taken
sash._ov: moulding stuck 1/2 in on by 3/16 in down for 1 1/2 in sashes, p.127: modelled as an ovolo 3/16 in
sash._glass: 21 oz sheet, about 1/10 in, Rivington Part III p.440
sash._src_bar_rebate_width_mm: Was 4.8, from Ellis p.127, whose line reads '5/8 in. bars, depth of rebates 3/16 in.; stouter bars, 1/4 in. deep': depths, not widths. Now 1/4 in wide: P6's putty band each side of the bar, (34.5 px bar - 15.1 px lit fillet) / 2 = 9.7 px / 1.53 = 6.3 mm (fillet 13.5 to 16.5 px over the same 7 rows); Riley p.382, 'the width of the rebate varies from a quarter of an inch to half an inch', the least taken. Leaves a fillet of 22.2 - 2 x 6.4 = 9.4 mm (P6: 15.1 px = 9.9 mm). The bar's rebate depth stays rebate_depth_mm, 6.4, which is Ellis's 1/4 in for stouter bars and is what window_design and target_drawing already give the bar. (Round 1 had given the bars the stiles' 3/8 in rebate each side; REVIEW.md.)
sash._side: 1/16 in play each side, Hasluck p.404 (round 1 had none: the stiles touched the pulley stiles)
sash._putty: front putty bevelled in every rebate outside the glass, Rivington Part II (1887) pp.418-420 glazing (SOURCES.md [5])
sash._hornface: Fig. 416 is a face view: the bracket keeps the stile's outer edge and narrows on its inner edge by a small step and an ogee to about 0.45 of the stile's width (step, ogee and foot scaled off the figure, not printed); round 1 read the ogee as cut through the depth (found by the fresh review, REVIEW.md)

sill._h: oak sill 1 5/8 in at the front, Fig. 399
sill._p: left a little wider on the outside than the frame, p.124 (not printed: 1/4 in taken)
sill._f: weathering about 3/4 in over the sash path, scaled Figs. 399, 403
sill._u: the 3/8 in step under the staff bead, Fig. 403

stone_sill._src: projects at least 2 in, throated, 5 or 6 in longer than the opening (Rivington Part I p.9); 4 to 6 in thick (Mitchell, Burrell exam texts): 5 in taken
